currency: USD nominal dollars of the stated year
description: US federal tax, retirement-account, Social Security, Medicare and ACA parameters for tax/benefit year 2026, with officially published 2027 values under `published_2027`. Every number was fetched from the source named in its `source` key (see `sources` and data/tax/SOURCES-federal.md). Engine convention: all dollar amounts are nominal for the stated year; index forward per each block's `indexing` flag.

conventions.brackets: Arrays of {up_to, rate}. `up_to` is the inclusive upper bound of taxable income taxed at `rate`; null = no upper bound. Marginal: income between the previous up_to and this up_to is taxed at `rate`.
conventions.married_separate: Included where the source gives it; the engine's primary statuses are the three above.

indexing_legend.c_cpi_u: Indexed annually by Chained CPI-U under IRC 1(f)(3) (12 months ending Aug 31 of prior year). Model with simulated CPI (optionally minus ~0.25-0.3 pt/yr chained-CPI wedge). Statutory rounding applies (see `rounding` where given).
indexing_legend.cpi_w: Indexed to CPI-W (Social Security COLA: Q3 over Q3).
indexing_legend.awi: Indexed to the SSA national Average Wage Index (two-year lag): value_Y = base * AWI[Y-2] / AWI[base_year-2]. Model with simulated wage growth.
indexing_legend.none: Frozen in nominal dollars by statute; NOT indexed. Real value erodes with simulated inflation.
indexing_legend.statutory_schedule: Changes on a fixed schedule written into statute (see the schedule in the block).
indexing_legend.program_cost: Set annually by the agency from projected program costs (Medicare premiums/deductibles). Model with health-cost inflation.
indexing_legend.premium_vs_income_growth: ACA applicable percentages: adjusted by the ratio of premium growth to income growth since 2013.
indexing_legend.market: Market-determined observation (premiums, deductibles); model with health-cost inflation.

income_tax.law_note: OBBBA (P.L. 119-21, 7/4/2025) sec. 70101 made the TCJA rate structure (10/12/22/24/32/35/37) permanent; sec. 70102 made the larger standard deduction permanent and raised the base amounts; personal exemption permanently $0 (sec. 70103).
income_tax.rounding: Brackets and standard deduction: rounded down to next lowest multiple of $50 (rounding rule recalled from IRC 1(f)(7)/63(c)(4), not re-fetched).

additional_standard_deduction_65_or_blin.note: Per condition (age 65+ and/or blind) per person. Applies only when taking the standard deduction.

long_term_capital_gains_brackets.note: Applies to net long-term capital gains and qualified dividends. Thresholds are TAXABLE INCOME levels: gains stack on top of ordinary taxable income; the portion of gains falling below the 0% ceiling is taxed at 0%, below the 15% ceiling at 15%, above at 20%. NIIT (3.8%) is separate.

alternative_minimum_tax.note: OBBBA sec. 70107: from 2026 the phase-out thresholds reset to $500k/$1M (indexed from 2027, base 2025) and the phase-out rate doubles from 25% to 50% (statute text, sec. 70107(c): 'by substituting 50 percent for 25 percent'; consistent with the Rev. Proc. complete-phaseout amounts: 90,100/0.5 = 180,200).

itemized_deduction_limitation.rule: IRC 68 as amended (OBBBA sec. 70111): itemized deductions reduced by 2/37 of the lesser of (a) itemized deductions or (b) taxable income (before this rule, plus itemized deductions) in excess of the start of the 37% bracket. Effectively caps the benefit of itemized deductions at 35%.

income_tax.kiddie_tax_note: 1,350 is the IRC 1(g)(4)(A)(ii)(I) amount (Rev. Proc. 2025-32 sec. 4.02). The kiddie tax applies to a child's net unearned income above TWICE this amount ($2,700 in 2026; $2,800 in 2027): the first 1,350 is covered by the dependent standard deduction and the next 1,350 is taxed at the child's rate.

net_investment_income_tax.base: lesser of net investment income or MAGI over threshold

additional_medicare_tax.base: Medicare wages + self-employment income over threshold (combined for joint filers)

fica.oasdi_wage_base_rounding: nearest $300; cannot fall; frozen in years with a zero COLA

self_employment.note: SE tax base = 92.35% of net SE earnings; OASDI portion capped at wage base less W-2 Social Security wages; half of SE tax is an above-the-line deduction; additional 0.9% Medicare tax applies above the thresholds and is not deductible.

child_tax_credit.refundable_formula: 15% of earned income over $2,500, capped at refundable max per child

indexing.refundable_max_per_child: c_cpi_u (base $1,400 in 2017 dollars, rounded down to $100)

child_tax_credit.note: OBBBA sec. 70104 made the credit permanent and set $2,200 for 2025; the 2026 inflation-adjusted amount is still $2,200. Phase-out: $50 per $1,000 (or fraction) of MAGI over the threshold.

child_and_dependent_care_credit.rate_schedule: 50% reduced 1 pt per $2,000 (or fraction) of AGI over $15,000, not below 35%; then reduced 1 pt per $2,000 ($4,000 joint) of AGI over $75,000 ($150,000 joint), not below 20%
child_and_dependent_care_credit.note: New rate schedule (OBBBA sec. 70405) and $7,500 dependent-care FSA limit (sec. 70404) apply from tax year 2026.

savers_credit_agi_limits.note: 2026 is the last year of the Saver's Credit for retirement contributions: for tax years beginning after 2026 it is replaced by the Saver's Match (IRC 6433, a 50% federal matching contribution up to $2,000 of contributions, paid into the account) per SECURE 2.0 sec. 103; see IRS Notice 2026-66 footnote 2. The 2027 AGI limits in Notice 2026-66 (joint 50,000/54,000/83,000) apply to the residual credit for ABLE contributions only.

senior_deduction.phase_out_rule: Each person's $6,000 is reduced by 6% of MAGI over the threshold (fully gone at $175,000 single / $250,000 joint).
senior_deduction.note: IRC 151(d)(5)(C). In addition to the regular additional standard deduction for 65+. Does not reduce MAGI for Social Security taxation, IRMAA or ACA purposes (it is a below-the-line deduction).

salt_cap.rule: cap_Y reduced by 30% of (MAGI - threshold_Y), but not below $10,000. Same cap for single, HoH and joint; half for married filing separately.
salt_cap.schedule_note: 2025 and 2026 amounts are written in IRC 164(b)(7). 2027-2029 = 101% of prior year (statute gives no rounding rule; values here are computed, flagged computed=true). Reverts to $10,000 for tax years beginning after 2029.

mortgage_interest.note: OBBBA sec. 70108 made the $750,000 limit permanent.

charitable.note: OBBBA sec. 70424 ($1,000/$2,000 non-itemizer cash-gift deduction, IRC 170(p)) and sec. 70425 (0.5%-of-AGI floor for itemizers).

employer_plans_401k_403b_457b_tsp.super_catch_up_note: Replaces (does not add to) the age-50 catch-up for those attaining age 60-63 during the year.

indexing.super_catch_up_ages_60_to_63: cpi_u (greater of $10,000 or 150% of 2024 regular catch-up, indexed)

employer_plans_401k_403b_457b_tsp.indexing_method_note: IRC 415(d): adjusted like Social Security COLA, using CPI-U Q3 over base-period Q3.

hsa.note: From 2026, ACA bronze and catastrophic exchange plans are treated as HSA-eligible HDHPs (OBBBA sec. 71307). Catch-up is per account holder (each 55+ spouse needs their own HSA). No contributions once enrolled in Medicare.

rule_of_55.applies_to: employer qualified plans (401(k), 403(b)) of the employer separated from, when separation occurs in or after the calendar year the employee reaches age 55

ordering: conversion/rollover contributions, first-in first-out (taxable portion of each conversion first)
roth_ira.qualified_distribution: After the 5-tax-year period beginning Jan 1 of the first year a contribution was made to any Roth IRA, AND age 59.5 (or death, disability, first-home up to $10,000 lifetime). Qualified distributions of earnings are tax-free.
roth_ira.conversion_five_year_rule: Each conversion has its own 5-tax-year clock (starting Jan 1 of the conversion year); withdrawing the taxable part of a conversion before the clock ends AND before age 59.5 incurs the 10% penalty (no income tax, already taxed). This is the basis of the Roth conversion ladder.

hsa_non_medical_penalty.note: IRC 223(f)(4): 20% additional tax on non-medical HSA distributions before age 65 (plus ordinary income tax); after 65 ordinary income tax only.

sepp_72t.max_interest_rate: greater of 5% or 120% of the federal mid-term rate for either of the two months preceding the first distribution
sepp_72t.must_continue_until: later of 5 years from first payment or age 59.5
sepp_72t.modification_penalty: 10% recapture on all prior payments plus interest
sepp_72t.life_expectancy_tables: Uniform Lifetime, Single Life or Joint and Last Survivor (26 CFR 1.401(a)(9)-9)

required_minimum_distributions.birth_year_1959_note: SECURE 2.0 drafting overlap: final regs (89 FR 58886, 7/19/2024) say 73 for those born 1951-1958 and 75 for those born 1960+, and reserve 1959; proposed regs treat 1959 as age 73. Encoded here as 73.
required_minimum_distributions.first_rmd_deadline: April 1 of the year after reaching the start age (later years: Dec 31)
required_minimum_distributions.calculation: RMD = prior Dec 31 balance / divisor for age attained in the distribution year
required_minimum_distributions.uniform_lifetime_table_effective: distribution years beginning on or after 2022-01-01
required_minimum_distributions.uniform_lifetime_table_note: Last row (age 120) applies to age 120 and older. Used unless the sole beneficiary is a spouse more than 10 years younger.

cola.note: The '2026 COLA' (2.8%) is effective with benefits for Dec 2025, paid Jan 2026; the '2027 COLA' (3.6%) is effective Dec 2026, paid Jan 2027.
cola.history_note: Key = year the COLA was determined (effective December of that year, first paid the following January; pre-1983 COLAs were effective June/July). Values in percent.

pia_formula.rule: PIA = 90% of AIME up to bend1 + 32% of AIME between bend1 and bend2 + 15% of AIME above bend2, using the bend points for the year the worker turns 62 (or dies/becomes disabled); round down to next lower $0.10. Then apply every COLA from the year of eligibility (age 62) onward.
pia_formula.family_maximum_factors_note: Factors 150/272/134/175% and the 2027 bend points confirmed against SSA 'Formula for Family Maximum Benefit' (source ssa_family_max); total rounded down to the next lower $0.10.

aime.rule: Index each year's capped earnings to AWI of the year the worker turns 60: indexed = min(earnings, wage_base[y]) * AWI[year_turn_60] / AWI[y]; earnings at age 60 and later taken at face value. Take the highest 35 years (zeros included), sum, divide by 420, round down to whole dollar.

maximum_taxable_earnings.note: OASDI contribution and benefit base 1937-2027. Amounts for 1937-1974 and 1979-1981 were set by statute.

full_retirement_age.note: fra_months = FRA in months (792 = 66y0m, 804 = 67y0m). People born on Jan 1 use the prior year. For survivor (widow/er) benefits add 2 to the birth year thresholds.

delayed_retirement_credit.note: No credit after age 70. Credits earned during a year are applied the following January (or at 70).

earnings_test.note: Applies only before FRA; year-of-FRA threshold counts only earnings in months before FRA. Withheld benefits are restored via recomputation at FRA (not lost).

benefit_taxation.provisional_income: AGI excluding Social Security + tax-exempt interest + 50% of Social Security benefits
benefit_taxation.formula: taxable = min(0.85*benefits, 0.85*max(0, PI - adjusted_base) + min(0.5*benefits, 0.5*(adjusted_base - base), 0.5*max(0, PI - base)))

spousal_benefit.rule: Spouse receives the greater of own retirement benefit or (own benefit + excess spousal top-up up to 50% of worker's PIA); worker must have filed. Deemed filing applies (cannot claim one and defer the other). No increase for claiming after FRA.

survivor_benefit.rule: Surviving spouse (married 9+ months) gets up to 100% of the deceased's benefit (including delayed credits) at survivor FRA, scaling linearly from 71.5% at age 60; survivor effectively keeps the larger of the two benefits. May claim survivor benefit and switch to own retirement benefit later (or vice versa).
survivor_benefit.widows_limit_note: If the deceased claimed early, survivor at FRA gets the larger of the deceased's reduced benefit or 82.5% of the deceased's PIA (figure recalled, not re-fetched).

trust_fund.note: Retirement benefits are paid from OASI (78% payable from Q4 2032 under current law); the combined OASDI figure (83% from 2034) is hypothetical because the funds cannot be merged without legislation. OASI payable share declines from 78% at depletion to 62% by 2100 (2026 Trustees summary, Table 8).

part_d.note: National base beneficiary premium; actual plan premiums vary. Annual increase capped at 6% through 2029 (IRA).

irmaa.lookback_note: 2026 premiums use MAGI from the 2024 tax return (AGI + tax-exempt interest).

indexing.top_tier_threshold: none (frozen at $500,000/$750,000 through 2027; indexed from 2028 - recalled, not re-fetched)
indexing.surcharges: program_cost. The TOTAL Part B premium in the five IRMAA tiers is about 1.4x, 2.0x, 2.6x, 3.2x, 3.4x the standard premium (beneficiary pays 35/50/65/80/85% of cost instead of 25%), so the SURCHARGE stored in part_b_surcharge_monthly is about 0.4x, 1.0x, 1.6x, 2.2x, 2.4x the standard premium (2026: 81.20/202.90 = 0.4). Part D surcharges scale with the Part D base beneficiary premium.

irmaa.tier_boundary_note: magi_over is exclusive, magi_up_to inclusive for tiers 1-4 ('greater than X and less than or equal to Y'); the top tier starts AT (>=) $500,000/$750,000, and for married_separate_lived_together AT (>=) the last magi_over ($391,000 in 2026, $388,000 in 2027), i.e. the preceding tier's magi_up_to is exclusive in those cases.

enhanced_subsidies_status.finding: The ARPA/IRA enhanced premium tax credits expired on 2025-12-31 and were NOT extended. For 2026 and 2027 coverage the original ACA schedule applies: credits only for household income from 100% to 400% of FPL, with no credit at all above 400% (the 'subsidy cliff').

premium_tax_credit.formula: PTC = max(0, benchmark SLCSP premium for the household - applicable_percentage * household MAGI). Within each band the percentage rises linearly from initial to final as income rises across the band.
premium_tax_credit.magi_definition: AGI + tax-exempt interest + non-taxable Social Security + excluded foreign income
premium_tax_credit.fpl_year_used: Coverage year Y uses the HHS poverty guidelines published in year Y-1 (2026 coverage -> 2025 guidelines; 2027 coverage -> 2026 guidelines).
premium_tax_credit.above_400_pct_fpl: no credit (applicable percentage undefined; household pays full premium)
premium_tax_credit.excess_advance_ptc_repayment_cap: none from tax year 2026 (OBBBA sec. 71305 repealed the repayment limits: all excess advance credit must be repaid)

federal_poverty_guidelines.alaska_hawaii_note: alaska_2026/hawaii_2026 apply to 2027 coverage; 2026 coverage uses alaska_2025/hawaii_2025 (ASPE poverty guidelines API, fetched 2026-11-17).

benchmark_premium.definition: National average second-lowest-cost silver plan monthly premium for a 40-year-old, weighted by county plan selections (before subsidy)
benchmark_premium.note: Scale to other ages with age_rating_curve: premium(age) = monthly_age_40 * factor(age) / factor(40). Varies widely by state and rating area.

age_rating_curve.description: Federal default standard age curve (in effect since plan year 2018), premium ratio relative to age 21 = 1.000; 3:1 max adult ratio. Ages 0-14 share one band; 64 means 64 and older. AL, DC, MA, MN, MS, NJ(small group), NY, OR, UT, VT use state curves or community rating.
age_rating_curve.child_rating_note: Only the three oldest covered children under 21 are charged.

average_deductible_2026.scope: HealthCare.gov plans, individual, combined medical+drug deductible

home_sale_exclusion.ownership_and_use_test: owned and used as main home for 2 of the 5 years before sale; once every 2 years

qualified_business_income_deduction.rule: Deduction = 20% of qualified business income (pass-through/sole-proprietor), limited to 20% of taxable income less net capital gain. Below the threshold no further limits; across the phase-in range the W-2 wage/property limits phase in and specified service trades (SSTB) phase out entirely.

estate_and_gift.basic_exclusion_note: $15,000,000 per person for 2026 set by OBBBA sec. 70106 (Rev. Proc. 2025-32 sec. 2.14); indexed after 2026.

published_2027.note: Officially published tax/benefit-year 2027 values (as of 2026-11-17). Same structure/semantics as the 2026 blocks above.

irmaa.lookback_note: 2027 premiums use MAGI from the 2025 tax return.

supplemental_wage_withholding.note: Flat federal income tax withholding on supplemental wages; 37% is mandatory on the part of a calendar year's supplemental wages above $1,000,000. Pub. 15 (2026): 'The withholding rate on supplemental wages remains 22% (37% if supplemental wages paid to an employee during the calendar year exceed $1 million).'

qualified_small_business_stock.note: IRC 1202(b)(1), (b)(4): gain excluded per issuer is capped at the greater of the dollar amount (less gain excluded in earlier years) or ten times basis; the engine applies the dollar amount only. The $15,000,000 is indexed from 2027 (1202(b)(5)); the engine holds it fixed, which understates the cap slightly in later years. Holding-period tiers (50% at 3 years, 75% at 4, 100% at 5 for stock acquired after July 4, 2025; 100% after 5 years for earlier stock) are constants in the code citing 1202(a).
